newsitem.title: USA: PSNH delays 355 MW unit restart to December.
newsitem.headline: PSNH delays 355 MW unit restart to December.

text.p: Public Service of New Hampshire (PSNH) said Tuesday it delayed until Dec 9 the restart of the 355 megawatt (MW) unit at its coal-fired Merrimack power station.
"It now an unanticipated shutdown because of a malfunction. It'll be down for at least 12 days," a PSNH spokesman said.

Merrimack's unit 2, scheduled to return to service this past weekend, stayed shut after a rotor problem was found in the generator, the spokesman said. It was originally shut Oct 25 for boiler maintenance.
Neighboring 125 MW Merrimack unit 1 was running at full output, he said.
The Merrimack units, near the town of Bow in central New Hampshire, produce 23 percent of the utility's power output.
Public Service of New Hampshire is a subsidiary of Northeast Utilities.
